title: Present perfect: forms and uses
intro: Read this before the questions on the present perfect and the past participle.

blocks.title: present perfect
items: **Form:** have / has + **past participle**: She **has finished**. I **have seen** it.
**Negative:** have / has + not + past participle: He **has not arrived** (hasn't arrived).
**Question:** Have / Has + subject + past participle: **Have** you **eaten**?
**Present perfect continuous:** have / has + **been** + verb-ing: I **have been waiting** for an hour.

blocks.title: the past participle
items: **Irregular verbs** must be learned: go, went, **gone**; see, saw, **seen**; write, wrote, **written**; take, took, **taken**; be, was or were, **been**; do, did, **done**; eat, ate, **eaten**; begin, began, **begun**; break, broke, **broken**; speak, spoke, **spoken**; give, gave, **given**; know, knew, **known**; buy, bought, **bought**; have, had, **had**.

blocks.title: when to use it
blocks.body:
1. Experience (ever, never): Have you ever seen a lion?
2. A past action with a result now: I have lost my keys.
3. A period that is not finished (this week, so far, since, for): I have lived here for five years.
4. Recent news (just, already, yet): She has just arrived.

blocks.title: the slips
items: Never use a finished time (yesterday, last year, in 2019, two days ago) with the present perfect: **I saw him yesterday**, not *I have seen him yesterday*.
**since** + a point in time (since Monday, since 2019). **for** + a length of time (for two years).
**has gone** (is still away) is not the same as **has been** (went and came back).
**yet** goes in questions and negatives. **already** goes in positive sentences.
